newsitem.title: UK: ICl at 21-month low on currency worries.
newsitem.headline: ICl at 21-month low on currency worries.

text.p: Shares in Imperial Chemical Industries Plc (ICI) hit their lowest level in almost two-years on Friday amid continued worries about the impact of a strong sterling on profits, traders said.
By 1405 GMT ICI was down 31p at 720, after earlier drooping to 715p, its lowest since March 1995.
BOC Group was also weak, down 21-1/2p at 859-1/2, while other weak shares with significant foreign operations were RMC Group Plc, down 43-1/2p at 896 and Siebe Plc, down 33p at 10.175 stg.

On Thursday, analysts at HSBC James Capel cut their forecasts for all chemical sector profits in 1997 and 1998 by around 4.5 percent, lopping 100 million pounds off expected earnings at ICI in both these years.
"Currency worries are still weighing on the chemical sector and there's a hangover from yesterday's downgrade," one market-maker said.
"It's on the front page of the FT (Financial Times) today which has brought in some sellers."

Internationally-oriented UK stocks have been battered by a wave of profit downgrades this week as analysts cut earnings forecasts on the back of sterling strength. Dealers said several foreign-earning companies were continuing to suffer.

The influential Lex column in the Financial Times warned on Friday that chemicals shares would be among the hardest hit. "The chemicals sector looks...vulnerable given an unpalatable cocktail of high exports and an inability to raise prices," it said.
It added that engineering firms BTR Plc, Smiths Industries Plc and GKN Plc would also be hit by sterling's strength as they "have substantial continental European exports and margins must suffer."
BTR Plc fell 8-1/2p to 253, Smiths Industries lost 20p to 798-1/2 and GKN dropped 22p to 992-1/2.
